title: Maternal disease, drugs and exposures: who needs referral

items.question: The mother has pregestational diabetes. What does AHA 2014 say about referral for fetal cardiac evaluation?
items.explanation: Pregestational diabetes, or diabetes diagnosed in the first trimester, is a Class I indication.

items.question: Gestational diabetes with HbA1c below 6%. What does AHA 2014 say about referral?
items.explanation: Gestational diabetes with HbA1c below 6% is listed as not indicated.

items.question: The mother has SSA/SSB autoantibodies and no previously affected child. What does AHA 2014 say about referral?
items.explanation: With a previously affected child referral is indicated (Class I). Without one it is reasonable (Class IIa).

items.question: The mother took NSAIDs in the third trimester. What does AHA 2014 say about referral?
items.explanation: NSAIDs in the third trimester are a Class I indication. NSAIDs in the first or second trimester are Class IIb.

items.question: Which SSRI is listed as a referral that may be considered?
items.explanation: Paroxetine is Class IIb. SSRIs other than paroxetine are listed as not indicated.

items.question: A mother had an infection other than rubella, with seroconversion only. What does AHA 2014 say about referral?
items.explanation: First-trimester rubella and infection with suspected fetal myocarditis are indications. Other infection with seroconversion only is not.
